# 3 Axial Skyrmions  
- Note that this reflection changes the sign of only one of the pion fields and so their definition of the relative phase differs by an addition of π in comparison with that of refs.[3, 12, 7]  
- In refs.[3, 12, 7], the antiSkyrmion is obtained by changing the sign of all three of the pion fields, which contrasts with the current definition  
- The definition used in this paper makes for a more natural comparison with the similar situation for monopoles  
- The profile function is zero at a radius s/2 from the centre of the Skyrmion (or antiSkyrmion), so the Skyrmion and antiSkyrmion are patched together in a continuous way, with the fields set to the vacuum outside each of the cores  

# Initial Conditions and Ansatz  
- In addition to the initial conditions using the simple ansatz (3.7), more sophisticated initial conditions were also used  
- These advanced initial conditions are based on the rational map ansatz [11]  
- The rational map ansatz employs an axially symmetric charge n map for improved accuracy  
- This approach allows for a more refined construction of Skyrmion configurations compared to the simple ansatz (3.7)
